brief.headline: SK Hynix overtakes Samsung as Korea's most valuable company; hyperscaler capex at $600B+ accelerates HBM tightness and DRAM/NAND pricing surge into Q2
brief.summary: <cite index="34-1,34-2,34-3">SK Hynix surpassed Samsung Electronics on June 23 to become South Korea's most valuable listed company with market cap of 2,080.4 trillion won ($1.35 trillion), driven by a 340%+ YTD rally on its dominant 61% HBM market share and AI supply dynamics</cite>. <cite index="35-1,35-8,35-11">Samsung announced a 90 trillion won buyback on June 24, sending its stock up ~10% to 340,500 won while SK Hynix gained 2.58% to 2,621,000 won after both fell 12% the prior session</cite>. <cite index="10-7,15-15,15-22">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 58–63% QoQ in Q2 2026 and NAND 70–75% QoQ as suppliers reallocate capacity to HBM and enterprise SSDs</cite>, <cite index="21-1,21-10">supported by Big Five hyperscaler capex exceeding $600 billion in 2026 (+36% YoY) with ~$450 billion tied to AI infrastructure</cite>. <cite index="28-1,28-3">TSMC's CoWoS capacity is expected to reach 115,000–140,000 wafers/month by end-2026 and ~170,000 wafers/month in 2027</cite>, with <cite index="32-5">Nvidia securing nearly 60% of 2026 CoWoS allocation</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="34-11">SK Hynix held 61% global HBM share in 2025 vs Samsung's 17% and Micron's 21%</cite>, cementing structural market-share advantage. <cite index="1-11,1-17">SK Hynix maintains 62% HBM shipment share as of Q2 2025 and is expected to capture ~70% of HBM4 for Nvidia's Rubin platform</cite>; <cite index="2-9,2-10">SK Hynix shipped 12-layer HBM4E samples to major customers on June 18</cite> while <cite index="39-26">Samsung shipped 12-layer HBM4E samples on May 29 and all three vendors passed Nvidia HBM4 qualification for Vera Rubin</cite>. Samsung buyback mechanically supportive near-term but <cite index="39-19">Samsung's HBM3E yield and qualification delays with Nvidia remain the proximate cause of the 61% vs 17% share gap</cite>. <cite index="34-20,34-21,34-22">SK Hynix DRAM output of ~589k wafers/month in 2026 trails Samsung's 691k, but SK Hynix is expanding 38% 2025–28 vs Samsung's 17.5%, narrowing the gap to <10% by 2028 from 23% in 2025</cite>. Long SK Hynix vs Samsung on HBM leverage, accelerating conventional DRAM share gains, and pure-play premium re-rating; watch Samsung's ability to convert HBM4 qualification into volume orders and close yield gap through 2H26.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="10-7,10-8">DRAM contract prices climbed 90–95% QoQ in Q1 2026 and are rising 58–63% in Q2 2026; NAND rose ~60% in Q1 and 70–75% in Q2</cite>. <cite index="11-22,11-24,11-25">Hyperscaler capex among top eight CSPs is projected to exceed $600B in 2026 (+40% YoY); HBM carries a 3-to-1 wafer conversion ratio vs DDR5, directly compressing general-purpose memory supply</cite>. <cite index="12-4,12-5">DRAM manufacturers reallocate advanced nodes and new capacity toward server DRAM and HBM to support AI server demand, significantly constraining supply to other applications</cite>. <cite index="1-20,1-21,1-22">Focused HBM investment improves general DRAM supply-demand as resources divert to HBM; server DDR5 module demand and HBM expected to form two main pillars of DRAM in 2026</cite>. <cite index="14-7">HBM capacity for 2026 is entirely sold out with manufacturers refusing new orders</cite>; <cite index="15-7">clear NAND shortage expected in 2026 with meaningful capacity expansion unlikely until late 2027 or 2028</cite>. Pricing unlikely to roll over before 2H27; structural tightness driven by hyperscaler AI buildout and capacity conversion to HBM.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-7,1-9">HBM3E expected to remain flagship product in 2026 and account for ~two-thirds of total HBM shipments, while HBM4 gradually increases share</cite>. <cite index="2-9,2-10,2-11">SK Hynix shipped 12-layer HBM4E samples on June 18 featuring 16Gbps per pin speed and >20% improved power efficiency</cite>; <cite index="6-1,6-4,6-6,6-7">Samsung started HBM4 mass production in February 2026 at Pyeongtaek, with SK Hynix also ramping around same time</cite>. <cite index="7-10,7-11,7-14,7-15">Nvidia testing 16-layer HBM for Q4 2026 delivery, even before 12-layer HBM4 reaches full commercial rollout expected in early 2026</cite>. <cite index="1-8">Nvidia Blackwell Ultra, Google, and AWS expanding proprietary ASIC-based AI chips and selecting HBM3E as optimal solution</cite>. <cite index="4-8">Reports indicate Samsung and SK Hynix plan ~20% HBM3E price hike for 2026 as Nvidia H200 and ASIC demand rises</cite>. Pricing power sustained through 2026; 12-layer HBM4 ramp in 2H26 for Nvidia Rubin (launch 2H26) will be key inflection for SK Hynix revenue mix upgrade and Samsung's ability to gain share.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix overtakes Samsung as most valuable Korean company on HBM dominance
news_pulse.implication: Structural shift in Korea equity landscape; SK Hynix now world's most valuable memory chipmaker on 340%+ YTD rally. HBM premium vs commodity DRAM drives valuation divergence; Samsung's diversified model (logic, foundry, consumer electronics) undervalued relative to pure-play memory exposure. Watch institutional flows into SK Hynix ADRs (HXSCL) and potential Nasdaq listing.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung announces 90 trillion won buyback; stock surges ~10% on June 24
news_pulse.implication: Epic buyback stabilizes Samsung after 12% single-day drop on June 23; KOSPI surged 3.26% on June 24. Mechanically supportive but does not address fundamental HBM share loss to SK Hynix. Samsung needs HBM3E/HBM4 volume ramps with Nvidia to justify valuation vs SK Hynix; buyback buys time but not market share.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity to reach 115k–140k wafers/month by end-2026, 170k in 2027
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS remains critical bottleneck for HBM-equipped AI accelerators. Nvidia locked ~60% of 2026 allocation; expansion into 2027 eases but doesn't eliminate supply constraint. SK Hynix leverages TSMC packaging partnership (12nm and 3nm base die for HBM4E) while Samsung uses in-house packaging; TSMC capacity allocation directly impacts SK Hynix vs Samsung relative supply ability.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler capex hits $600B+ in 2026 (+36% YoY); ~$450B tied to AI infrastructure
news_pulse.implication: Amazon $200B, Google $175–185B, Microsoft $110–120B capex in 2026. Roughly half is servers/chips (Nvidia GB200/GB300, HBM3E/HBM4); rest is datacenter shells, power, networking. Memory (HBM + DDR5) consumption scales faster than supply expansion; structural bid under Samsung/SK Hynix pricing and volume through 2027. Cloud AI revenue real and accelerating—demand not speculative.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contract prices +58–63% QoQ in Q2 2026; NAND +70–75% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: Q1 2026 saw DRAM +90–95% QoQ, NAND +55–60%; Q2 pricing acceleration for NAND outpaces DRAM for first time. Server DRAM >60% QoQ; enterprise SSD demand shows no signs of slowing. HBM capacity reallocation tightens conventional DRAM/NAND supply; CSPs securing capacity via long-term agreements. Pricing unlikely to peak before late 2026; Samsung/SK Hynix operating leverage inflection continues.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix ships 12-layer HBM4E samples (16Gbps, >20% power efficiency gain)
news_pulse.implication: HBM4E (enhanced HBM4) sampling on June 18 reinforces SK Hynix technical lead. 48GB capacity in 12-layer stack; 17% improved heat resistance vs HBM4. SK Hynix maintaining generational advantage into HBM4E (likely 2027 mass production); positions company for next wave of Nvidia/hyperscaler orders. Samsung also sampled 12-layer HBM4E on May 29 but SK Hynix holds incumbency and yield advantage.

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia testing 16-layer HBM for Q4 2026 delivery; 12-layer HBM4 ramp ongoing
news_pulse.implication: Nvidia pulling forward generational transition before 12-layer HBM4 reaches full commercial rollout. 16-layer HBM4 (or HBM4E) discussions exploratory but signal accelerating memory roadmap for Rubin (2H26 launch). Performance evaluation expected before Q3 2026. Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron all racing to meet requirements; technical complexity (hybrid bonding, thermal management) favors incumbents with mature MR-MUF processes (SK Hynix) or early hybrid bonding adoption (Samsung).

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix in talks with Korea govt on new semiconductor cluster in Honam region
news_pulse.implication: Potential front-end fab and packaging investments exceeding 200 trillion won (Samsung) and possibly larger for SK Hynix in Honam (southwestern Korea). Speculative reports raise questions about Yongin cluster timeline. Presidential adviser notes AI demand may require accelerating new fab construction to 2034–35 (vs original plans). If confirmed, signals both companies see sustained AI/HBM demand justifying massive incremental capex; bullish for multi-year memory cycle.

Samsung ADR (SSNLF) and SK Hynix ADR (HXSCL) likely see increased vol and wider bid-ask spreads; watch for institutional repositioning into SK Hynix on pure-play HBM thesis. USD/KRW stable per payload but Korea equity vol spike may impact carry dynamics.

SK Hynix management commentary or filings addressing market-cap milestone, Nasdaq listing timeline, and HBM4E mass production schedule; any customer announcements (Nvidia Rubin allocation, Google TPU v7 wins)
